newsitem.title: UK: Rogerson to leave BG but departure "not imminent".
newsitem.headline: Rogerson to leave BG but departure "not imminent".

text.p: Philip Rogerson, deputy chairman of BG plc, will be leaving the company in due course but his departure is not imminent, a spokeswoman for the company said on Monday.
"In due course he will be leaving, that's no secret, but there's no immediacy for him to do so," she said. "He continues as deputy chairman and his advice and experience are greatly valued."

Rogerson was appointed deputy chairman in charge of two specific projects, she said. These were the demerger of British Gas into BG plc and Centrica plc, and the MMC enquiry into the price controls imposed by industry regulator Ofgas on BG pipeline arm Transco.

The MMC was widely perceived to have come down on the side of Ofgas in its report, published last week. Controversy immediately surrounded Rogerson's role in the enquiry as he had earlier referred to the original Ofgas proposal as "one of the biggest smash and grab raids ever."

The BG spokeswoman added that Rogerson still has some work left to do tying up details from the MMC report. His contract with BG terminates automatically on 31 December 1999, but he has the right to terminate his employment after January 1998 by giving one month's notice.
But in some circumstances it would be possible for him to leave early, she added.
